High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood can extend the current term by 12 months at the proposed discounted commit, contingent on the EU node cutover being completed in Q4.
- Provide a runbook and estimated downtime windows for the EU cutover (we need a max 2-hour user-impact window).
- Outline how cross-region failover will work for bursts in APAC (warm standby vs. hot mirroring), and any incremental costs.

We can loop in procurement, but wanted to align on ops feasibility first. Can you circulate a consolidated plan and SOW update?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Renewal window & EU node cutover / APAC activation — technical notes

Grace / team — thanks for the ping. Quick technical summary from Infra/Delivery:

- EU sovereign node cutover: feasible in a staged sequence — provision new EU node, replicate model artifacts, run shadow traffic for 48 hours, then perform final cutover during a scheduled 2-hour maintenance window.
- We can keep KV cache warm using prefix mirroring; expected cold-start token latency impact ~1.2s for first user requests but normalizes quickly.
- Rollback option: DNS + routing rollback within 20 mins; full traffic rollback <60 mins if needed.

Pre-cutover checklist (attachment): 
- Provision EU compute (region-specific sizing)
- Model validation on EU node (end-to-end tests)
- Data residency confirmation & access control review
- Monitoring and alerting (traces + token-level cost telemetry)

Attachment: EU_node_spec.xlsx (xlsx)

We recommend a three-week staging cadence (provision -> shadow -> cutover) to minimize risk. For APAC, warm standby with on-demand burst is the likely cost-effective model; hot mirroring can be scoped if Medivia wants zero-latency regional primaries at higher cost.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
